data.description:
## What is wrong

`tests/integration/test_similar_tickets_scale.py:240`, in `test_the_cold_catch_up_cost_at_that_scale_is_emitted_as_a_number`, ends with:

```python
assert isinstance(p95, float)
assert p95 > 0.0
```

Any wall-clock sample satisfies both unconditionally. A duration measured with a monotonic clock is a float, and it is positive. There is no behaviour of the code under test that makes this test fail — not a regression in catch-up cost, not an incorrect p95 computation, not a catch-up that silently indexes nothing. It is a measurement emitter wearing a test's name.

Found by the Gerrit `LLM-Review` bot on change 3211 patchset 2 (advisory, non-blocking). No change was made under 47c8 because it was the keystone blocking three tickets and resetting its gates for a non-blocking test-naming issue was not worth the round trip.

## Why it matters beyond the test file

The number this test emits is the number ADR 0122 cites as rebar's cold-catch-up p95 (ticket `weaponed-handheld-centipede`). A figure that enters the binding design record should come from something that can fail if the figure is wrong. Today nothing checks it against anything.

## The two things to settle

**Whether the name claims more than the body delivers.** The test is named for emitting a number, and emitting a number is what it does, so one defensible resolution is that it is correctly named and simply is not a test. The other is that a scale suite should assert something about scale.

**What a non-vacuous assertion would even be.** A wall-clock ceiling is the obvious candidate and is the wrong one: 47c8 removed exactly such a budget from this file after a 500 ms criterion measured 107 ms on the development host and 545 ms on `macos-latest`. Whatever replaces the vacuous pair must be a counted invariant or a same-host ratio, consistent with how `WARM_TO_COLD_RATIO` already works at `tests/integration/test_similar_tickets_scale.py:12`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test either asserts a property that can fail for some behaviour of the code under test, or is renamed and documented so its name does not claim to test one.
- [ ] If an assertion is added, it is a counted invariant or a same-host ratio, not an absolute wall-clock budget. Checked by: the assertion referencing no fixed millisecond constant.
- [ ] If an assertion is added, a test demonstrates it fails when the invariant is violated. Checked by: that test.
- [ ] The file is swept for the same shape, so a sibling vacuous assertion is not left behind. Checked by: naming in the change what was found.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Provenance

Carried from the change 3211 patchset 2 review and from a comment recorded on `weaponed-handheld-centipede`, which consumes the number this test emits.
data.title: The cold-catch-up scale test asserts only that a duration is a positive float, so it cannot fail
